findings.title: Scope matches the slice plan entry; nothing assigned to 129 is dropped
findings.description:
The slice plan entry (line 79) asks for:
- **Part A:** port to `openai_codex`, bundled binary first with PATH as fallback, a `codex` optional extra, effort through `ReasoningEffort` (#171), and per-turn usage.
- **Part B:** a missing-package error, a doctor row, a model-list marker, and a README update.
- **Part C:** interactive login as a strategy capability, browser and `--device-code` flows, account email/plan in status, and logout.

Every item appears in Technical Scope (lines 32–38), and the success criteria (lines 188–205) cover each one. The exclusions (no squadron token store, no `login_api_key`, no change to the `AuthStrategy` Protocol) are consistent with the plan's "squadron keeps no token store of its own."

findings.title: Consistent with the architecture's "no unified auth" principle
findings.description: `100-arch.orchestration-v2.md:243` says squadron does not unify authentication. The design addresses this directly. `InteractiveLogin` is an optional capability that only the Codex strategy implements. It hands all work to the Codex runtime and stores no credentials. Leaving the architecture's auth table untouched until a second provider adopts the capability is a reasonable, proportionate choice.

findings.title: Dependency directions and layer boundaries are correct
findings.description:
- The Protocols live in `providers/auth.py` and `providers/base.py`. The Codex provider implements them, and the CLI uses them only through `isinstance` checks.
- The `notify` callback (line 168) keeps Rich out of the provider layer.
- SDK imports happen only inside functions, in `runtime.py`, `login.py` and `agent.py`, so the default install still imports cleanly.
- D3 and D9 avoid the profile-name and auth-type string checks that slice 128 removed.

findings.title: Failure modes for logout, and for login when the runtime won't start, are not specified
findings.description:
The failure-mode table covers the Codex turn in detail. Login gets only three items at line 138: timeout, `success=False`, and `account()` failure. Two new I/O paths are not covered:

- **`AsyncCodex.logout()`.** It spawns the runtime (line 82), but no timeout bounds it. None of `codex.turn_timeout_s`, `login_timeout_s` or `account_timeout_s` applies. The design does not say what happens when logout hangs, when the SDK raises, or when the runtime fails to start.
- **Runtime start or `initialize` failure during `sq auth login`.** This covers the package being missing or no binary being found when the user runs the login command, before any handle exists. Functional requirement line 190 says any `openai-oauth` use must show the install command, but the login path never states that it calls `resolve_codex_runtime()` first.

Both are required by the project's failure-mode rule (`review-code.md`: every new I/O path needs hang, timeout and disconnect handling that is observable and tested).

**Fix:** add a short "Failure Modes — Login/Logout" table. Bound `logout()` with `codex.account_timeout_s`, or say why it doesn't need a bound. Route login and logout through `resolve_codex_runtime()` so they fail with the same install hint. Add the matching tests to line 199.

findings.title: The doctor's login check duplicates the strategy's validity logic and can disagree with `sq auth status`
findings.description:
Line 172 says the `codex provider` row reports "login state from `auth.json` presence." Line 232 keeps an open outcome: if the `OPENAI_API_KEY` fallback works, `OAuthFileStrategy` reports a key-only environment as authenticated. In that case `sq auth status` would say authenticated while `sq doctor` says "not logged in". The two commands would disagree, and the validity rule would live in two places.

D9 already takes care to route the extra-missing hint through one abstraction. Login state should get the same treatment.

**Fix:** have the doctor row read `is_valid()` / `active_source()` from the resolved `OAuthFileStrategy`. Neither spawns a subprocess, so the "no subprocess in doctor" constraint still holds. Drop the separate `auth.json` presence check.

findings.title: The version upper bound is stated as both decided and open
findings.description: D1 specifies `openai-codex>=0.159.3,<1`, which already includes a cap. Line 231 then says the upper bound "is not decided here; PM to say whether to cap." Pick one. Keeping `<1` as written and deleting the open item at line 231 removes the ambiguity without adding a decision gate.

findings.title: Two new Protocols have one implementer each and no planned consumers
findings.description:
The frontmatter (line 7) and Provides-to-Other-Slices (lines 178–181) say no planned slice uses `InteractiveLogin`, `ExtraRequirement` or `CodexRuntime`.

- **`InteractiveLogin`** is justified. The slice plan requires "a capability on the strategy, not a profile-name check."
- **`ExtraRequirement`** is also defensible. It replaces a hard-coded `"openai-oauth"` check in `sq model list`, and each Protocol is a single small interface.

This is acceptable. Keep both minimal, and don't add anything to them for hypothetical future providers.

findings.title: Slice 931 dependency is not in the plan entry but is justified
findings.description: The plan entry lists only `[128]`. The design adds slice 931 (`AgentConfig.effort`, `applies_effort`, `core/usage.py`), which is where the effort and usage features the plan entry asks for are implemented. The dependency is correct. The slice plan's Dependencies field could be updated to match.
